newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks end down, small-caps active.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks end down, small-caps active.

text.p: Jakarta stocks ended down on Tuesday, despite active local speculative buying of property stocks, due to profit-taking in selected big-caps, brokers said.
The Jakarta composite index fell 2.95 points, or 0.44 percent, to close at 672.87 points. Advancers led decliners by 56 to 54 with 73 issues unchanged.
Total turnover was estimated at 660 billion rupiah against 620 billion rupiah on Monday.
"The market was quite active, with trading dominated by local players who were chasing small-caps, particularly in the property sector," one broker said.
Brokers said the trading suspension of small-cap tourism firm Bayu Buana did not deter local speculators from going on a buying spree of small-capped stocks.
Bayu was suspended shortly after the open as the firm failed to answer on time the exchange's query following a 25-percent rise in the stock on Monday, an exchange official said.
Bayu was allowed to resume trading about one hour later after the exchange received confirmation from the firm that it had no new plans which had not been announced.
Bayu closed unchanged at 1,250 rupiah in active trading, with some 20 million shares changing hands.

Property firm Bakrieland, formerly Elang Realty, was the most active, with 71 million shares traded, as it rose 125 rupiah to close at 1,900 rupiah on reports of a proposed rights issue, brokers said.

Another small property firm Modern Land rose 175 rupiah to 3,875 rupiah, also in active trading, due mostly to speculative reasons, brokers said. Modern Land posted a net profit of 14.2 billion rupiah in 1996 against 23.0 billion rupiah in 1995.
Losers included heavyweights Gudang Garam, Sampoerna, Semen Gresik and Telkom on profit-taking, brokers said.
